title: Cohort Omega retrospective + escape-hatch plan
content:
Purpose:
This is the retrospective and immediate runbook ("escape-hatch") for Cohort Omega installs (six customers performed between 2027-03-01 and 2027-03-07). We focused on VPC+on-prem variants where customers had flaky DNS, intermittent NFS mounts, and non-standard BGP peering behaviour. This doc captures observed failure modes, customer-impacting blockers, mitigation patterns we validated during the week, and the short-term escape-hatch play to keep services healthy while we land long-term fixes.

Summary of incidents observed (topline):
- Repeated worker node kubelet crashes tied to corrupted cgroup entries after local NFS remounts (Customers CO-2, CO-5). Causes intermittent pod eviction and KV cache warm failures.
- Unexpected BGP session flap with two customers where the edge router re-announced low-priority routes every 7–12 minutes; manifested as packet loss for gRPC control plane (CO-3).
- DNS resolution returning mixed results from split-horizon setups: customers' internal DNS returned stale SRV records for control-plane endpoints during a 2–3 hour window (CO-1, CO-4).
- Large cold-start token spike due to cache coldness after mass pod restarts; correlated to autoscaler burst events (CO-2).
- One customer experienced identity/MTLS handshake failures due to reversed cert CN ordering in their HSM workflow (CO-6).

What we tried during installs (attempted mitigations):
- Isolated the NFS repro by pre-creating mounts with systemd automount + reduced timeouts; introduced a wrapper that gracefully unmounts and drains pods before NFS remount.
- For BGP: pushed a temporary route-filter on our edge (AS-path length > threshold) and asked customer to lock local router timers to longer hold; validated while watching route churn for 4 hours.
- DNS: introduced a short-lived local dnsmasq cache daemon on the node to avoid stale SRV lookups during churn windows.
- For cache coldness: primed KV cache by replaying recent traffic traces (sanitized) and using a staged rollout that pins a % of capacity to warm instances.
- MTLS/HSM: created a test harness to validate CN ordering and certificate chain before installing, plus an explicit pre-flight HSM cert check.

Impact assessment (customer facing):
- CO-2 and CO-5 saw service degradations (2–6 minutes of elevated 5xx) during the immediate incident windows. CO-3 had higher latency for control operations for ~90 minutes until BGP stabilised. CO-1/CO-4 had intermittent lookup failures during maintenance hours only. CO-6 had one failover event where the system temporarily used hosted fallback.

Root-cause analysis (short):
- Many issues were triggered by sequence interactions: customer infra (NFS flakiness, BGP configs, split DNS) + our aggressive autoscaler + assumptions in the node provisioning hooks (we assumed clean unmounts).
- The installation pre-flight checks are necessary but insufficient: they lacked a quick BGP sanity check and a deterministic NFS health probe.

Escape-hatch plan (immediately actionable, tiered):
1) Immediate (within hours) — Protect customer traffic and avoid cascading restarts:
   - Enable hosted fallback for affected routes: automated ephemeral routing to hosted inference for 0–10% traffic if control-plane handshake failures exceed threshold for >2m. Owner: Owen Patel. Due: 2027-03-10.
   - Deploy node-side automount wrapper universally for affected installs: systemd unit that will mark node Unschedulable before mount/unmount. Owner: Jin Park. Due: 2027-03-10.
   - Push route filter rule to our peering edge (temporary) to dampen rapid re-announcements; clear after stability window. Owner: Samir Alvarez + Networking. Due: 2027-03-09 EOD.

2) Near-term (days) — Prevent common triggers and add observability:
   - Add BGP sanity check into preflight: establish a short-lived BGP session to ensure routes are stable for 10m. Owner: Lena Morozov. Due: 2027-03-16.
   - Add NFS health probe to preflight and to node agent that can convert flaky mounts into read-only mounts (fail-open). Owner: Maya Chen. Due: 2027-03-15.
   - Add a DNS validation step that queries SRV and A records from both customer resolver and an independent resolver; surface divergence in Console during install. Owner: Devex team. Due: 2027-03-18.

3) Medium term (weeks) — Systemic fixes:
   - Autoscaler policy change: add a soft-rate limit on mass-scale-up events when cache-priming remaining < X tokens to avoid cold-token storms. Work tracked in INF-3221. Owner: Serving-runtime. Due: 2027-04-05.
   - Improve KV cache priming tooling to use sampled traffic replay with customer-supplied obfuscation; integrate into install pipeline. Owner: Applied-ML. Due: 2027-04-01.
   - Harden MTLS/HSM preflight and integrate an HSM cert validator that verifies CN ordering. Owner: Security & Private-deploy. Due: 2027-03-30.

Open action items and owners (compact):
- Owen: implement hosted-fallback circuit and add metric (fallback-activated) to Console dashboards. Due 2027-03-10.
- Jin: ship automount systemd wrapper and rollout to Omega installs. Due 2027-03-10.
- Samir: temporary peering filters + postmortem on BGP flaps; coordinate with NOC. Due 2027-03-09 EOD.
- Lena: spec BGP 10m sanity preflight PR and add unit tests. Due 2027-03-16.
- Maya: draft NFS read-only fallback probe and test harness. Due 2027-03-15.
- Applied-ML: prototype cache priming replay tool (sanitized). Due 2027-04-01.
- Security: HSM cert validator blueprint and integration ticket. Due 2027-03-30.

Notes from the install floor (raw, informal):
- "We saw a pattern where NFS flake -> kubelet OOM-ish symptoms -> autoscaler tries to replace pods -> massive cache regen -> token spike" (Jin).
- "Customer CO-3 had an old vendor config that re-enabled route-refresh on their eBGP session; once we forced no-route-refresh and filtered short AS-paths it settled." (Samir).
- "dnsmasq local cache trick bought us ~20–40 minutes of stability during the SRV churn window — but it's brittle. Must not be a long-term crutch." (Lena).

Suggested updates to install checklist (proposed):
- Add BGP sanity check checkbox + logs capture
- Record NFS mountbench (timeout, latency) and require < Xms median before proceeding
- HSM: run CN-order test vector
- Schedule installs outside customer's network change windows (02:00–04:00 local) when feasible

Follow-ups and coordination requests:
- NOC: please retain full BGP RIB snapshots for CO-3 and CO-5 between 2027-03-01 and 2027-03-08. Ticketed under INF-3140.
- Support: for customers with hosted-fallback active, surface a clear message in Console (red banner) and create a short runbook for their support reps. Owner: Support ops.
- Product: decide whether to add a "safe-mode" option at install time that pins a % of hosted capacity for warm warm-starts.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands (shared from floor)
- Check NFS latency: time dd if=/dev/zero of=/mnt/testfile bs=1M count=64
- BGP neighbor watch: watch -n 2 "vtysh -c 'show bgp neighbors json'"
- DNS SRV diff: dig +short @<customer-resolver> _control._tcp.example.com SRV; dig +short @8.8.8.8 _control._tcp.example.com SRV
- Force node unschedulable and drain in one step: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as live runbook until 2027-03-20; after that consolidate learnings to confluence:private-deploys/cohort-omega-postmortem.

End of notes.
